edits.text: When one candidate splits a verb (or auxiliary) from its required object/complement and the other splits earlier adjunct/subject material, prefer the cut that keeps the verb with its complement.
edits._was: - When one cut falls between a verb and its obligatory object/complement and another falls earlier within pre-verbal adjunct material, prefer the later cut after the complement.

edits.text: When one candidate splits a verb (or auxiliary) from its required object/complement and the other splits earlier adjunct/subject material, prefer the cut that keeps the verb with its complement.

- Does the right-side begin a required complement that completes the left predicate (a 'that' clause, a 'because' clause, an infinitival 'to' phrase used as complement, or an immediately following noun/pronoun object)? Keep the verb or auxiliary together with the complement that completes it; most harmful when the marker separates a verb from an immediately contiguous 'that/because/to' clause or noun phrase object, mild when the following material is optional or parenthetical.
